docs.title: guard-core-jvm
docs.text:
Kotlin/JVM port of the guard-core engine: the framework-free detection engine, the facade artifact that adapters integrate, and the conformance harness that proves behavior parity against the guard-core spec 4.1.0 corpus.

  • Spec version targeted: 4.1.0 (corpus regenerated at engine 4.3.2; provenance in the conformance README)
  • Parity status: every-feature matrix (880 rows: 826 FULL / 54 IDIOMATIC / 0 PARTIAL / 0 MISSING) and the jvm column of the spec section table
  • Mirror statement: guard-core-jvm 4.3.2 mirrors guard-core 4.3.2; versions move in lockstep
  • Maven group ID: com.guard-core (Kotlin packages com.guardcore.*)

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text:
The adapters implement the facade protocols for their framework's native request/response types and contain no security logic of their own: every decision is the engine's, and every adapter drives the same 17-check pipeline, byte-exact response factory, and per-route decorator resolution.

Adapter Repo Envelope Idiom spring-boot-guard Guard-Core/spring-boot-guard Spring Boot 3.x (WebMVC servlet filter, pre-routing so unmatched paths are also enveloped) GuardFilter + @Guard* annotations (25 decorator factories), guard.* properties binding all 129 SecurityConfig fields (object-typed fields through SecurityConfigCustomizer beans) ktor-guard Guard-Core/ktor-guard Ktor 3.x (custom plugin hook at the Plugins phase for the required short-circuit; response side on ResponseBodyReadyForSend) install(GuardCore) + GuardRouteDecorator, suspend-native guard-agent-jvm Guard-Core/guard-agent-jvm Telemetry sidecar behind the facade's AgentProtocol sink seam buffering, transport, circuit breaker, Redis persistence, AES-GCM + HMAC signing, redaction, dynamic rules

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The engine and facade mirror guard-core releases (4.3.2). The adapters start a fresh family version at 1.0.0 and pin the engine artifact version; the agent mirrors guard-agent (3.2.2). In CI, the adapters run against the engine at a pinned ref (the ecosystem-gate workflow in this repo runs both adapters' suites on every engine PR and master push), and the pins move to the released engine tag at train time.

docs.title: Writing a new adapter
docs.text:
1. Implement the protocols in com.guardcore.protocols for the native request/response types: request surface (headers, path, method, client IP, bounded body read), response surface (status, headers, tee-able body for behavioral return patterns), and the middleware protocol.
  2. Drive GuardCore (the facade middleware) per request; short-circuit on a block response before the handler runs; run the response path after it.
  3. Surface the decorator factories in the framework's idiom (annotations, plugins, interceptors - syntax, not substitutes).
  4. Re-export SecurityConfig and the user-facing types from the adapter package (the guard/__init__.py convention): consumers import from the adapter, never from the engine coordinates directly.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
The API reference is the KDoc surface of the two published artifacts, generated with Dokka. The facade is the integration artifact; the engine is the framework-free detection core.

Generate the HTML reference locally:

docs.title: Facade (com.guard-core:guard-core)
docs.text:
Entry point and wiring (package com.guardcore):

  • GuardCore - the facade middleware: construction over a SecurityConfig, lazy handler initialization, per-request dispatch through the 17-check pipeline, and the response path (behavioral return rules, metrics, security headers, CORS).
  • SecurityConfig / SecurityConfigBuilder - the 129-field configuration (Configuration); construction and assignment run the reference's validator chain with byte-matched rejection messages.
  • DetectionResult - the verdict type (threats, attack types, categories, scores).

Protocols (package com.guardcore.protocols, 8 files, the section 01 porting-contract equivalents): RequestProtocol, ResponseProtocol, MiddlewareProtocol and the middleware surface protocols, RedisProtocol, GeoIpProtocol, CloudIpStoreProtocol, AgentProtocol. Framework adapters implement these; nothing in the facade imports a framework.

Handlers (package com.guardcore.handlers): RedisManager, RateLimitManager (+ ThresholdBans), IpBanManager (+ bans/queries/migration), IpInfoManager, CloudManager (+ fetchers, registry, IP stores), SecurityHeadersManager, CorsHandler, BehaviorTracker, DynamicRuleManager, SusPatternsRegistry, and the seams (HandlerSeams) that let adapters inject implementations.

Core (package com.guardcore.core): the 17 security checks in fixed order (checks), the event bus with the guard-agent envelope and metrics (events), initialization, behavioral processing, validation, responses, bypass, and routing.

Decorators (package com.guardcore.decorators): SecurityDecorator with the 25 per-feature factories (rate limiting, access control, authentication, content filtering, behavioral analysis, honeypot, and so on), 1:1 with the reference's parameter surface.

Java bridges (package com.guardcore.java): JavaBridges exposes xBlocking (the unasync analog) and xFuture variants next to the suspend-primary API so Java-only consumers need no coroutine dependency.

docs.title: Engine (com.guard-core:guard-core-engine)
docs.text:
Package com.guardcore.engine (framework-free; kotlin-stdlib is its only dependency):

  • The PyRe layer: python-grammar fail-closed regex parser (sre AST), pattern translation + flag mapping, and python match semantics over java.util.regex.
  • The ReDoS static-safety chain: 25 modules ported 1:1 (IntervalSet through CostArbiter), plus hard match deadlines via DeadlineCharSequence and the validation cache.
  • The detection core: compiler, preprocessor, truncation, base64/encoding decoders, scan window, binary-prefix islands, semantic analyzer, monitor, and the python-unicode tables.
  • SusPatterns: the 157-row pattern table (byte-identical with the reference), matchers per source context, and the registry.

The engine has no public configuration surface: the facade's SecurityConfig drives it (the detection knobs are documented under Configuration).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: How the workspace maps to the guard-core behavioral spec sections. The behavioral spec is normative for observable behavior; internal architecture is free, and this page is where the JVM port's structure is documented.

docs.title: Module layout
docs.text:
guard-core-jvm/
├── guard-core-engine/        framework-free detection core (kotlin-stdlib only)
│   └── com.guardcore.engine  PyRe (parser/translation/semantics), redos chain,
│                             detection core, suspatterns tables
├── guard-core/               the facade (the adapter integration artifact)
│   └── com.guardcore         config, protocols, handlers, core, decorators, java bridges
├── guard-core-conformance/   the spec 4.1.0 corpus runner (unpublished)
└── guard-core-benchmark/     JMH cost-ceiling benchmarks (unpublished)

The engine/facade split mirrors guard-core-rs (framework-free crate + facade) and guard-core-go (single-package engine): nothing in guard-core-engine imports coroutines, Lettuce, or any framework, so the detection core can be embedded with no transport dependencies at all.

docs.title: Mapping to the spec sections
docs.text: Spec section JVM surface 01 contract com.guardcore.protocols (request, response, middleware, bounded reads; 8 files, 1:1 with protocols/) 02 config com.guardcore.config.SecurityConfig + ConfigFieldRegistry (129 fields, field-for-field) 03 pipeline com.guardcore.core.checks (17 checks, fixed order) 04 detection com.guardcore.engine (PyRe layer, deadline pools, monitor) 05 content pipeline com.guardcore.engine (decode chain, scan window, truncation, semantic analyzer) 06 suspatterns com.guardcore.engine (157-row table, matchers) + handlers.SusPatternsRegistry 07 rate limiting handlers.RateLimitManager + RateLimitScript + ThresholdBans (Redis Lua byte-exact) 08 redis schema handlers.RedisManager (Lettuce; keys/prefixes byte-exact, interop-tested) 09 ip bans handlers.IpBanManager + bans/queries/migration 10 cloud/geo handlers.CloudManager + fetchers/registry + IpInfoManager (MaxMind) 11 responses/headers core.responses + handlers.SecurityHeadersManager + CorsHandler 12 behavior/events core.behavioral + handlers.BehaviorTracker + core.events (bus, envelope, metrics)

docs.title: The async model
docs.text: The reference is asyncio-based; the JVM port is coroutine-based. suspend functions map 1:1 to the asyncio source; blocking scan pools (spec section 04) map to dedicated dispatchers with bounded parallelism; and the facade exposes Java-idiomatic entry points (xBlocking for blocking callers, xFuture for CompletableFuture consumers) - the unasync sync-mirror analog, confined to entry points. These are idiom mappings, not omissions: the every-feature matrix classifies each as IDIOMATIC with the reference anchor.

docs.title: Regex engine and ReDoS posture
docs.text: java.util.regex (backtracking, semantics close to Python re), with the Go posture layered on top: hard match deadlines via DeadlineCharSequence (the MatchTimeout analog), the full static-safety chain (25 _redos_* modules, cost arbiter, fail-closed strays), and the pattern ledger (conformance/, 158 entries, every corpus pattern compiling as-is or carrying a corpus-verified translation; a pattern with neither fails CI).

docs.title: Conformance and gates
docs.text: guard-core-conformance runs the vendored corpus (byte-identical fixtures, regenerated from the reference engine, never hand-written). The fullCorpusGate task pins the totals (375 cases + 9 cost budgets): a red suite blocks merge, a growing ledger is red, and a listed cost workload that returns under ceiling also fails (fail-closed xfail manifests). See the conformance README.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Every SecurityConfig field with its type, default, and effect. The canonical field names are the snake_case python names (the cross-language interop surface, spec 02): the Kotlin properties are the camelCase forms, and adapters bind them idiomatically (Spring relaxed binding maps guard.redis-url to redisUrl; Ktor takes the builder or the Kotlin property names). Types and defaults are normative; a conformant build with default config behaves as the reference with default config.

Generated by docs/tools/w8d_config_docs.py from ConfigFieldRegistry.kt (the ported reference field table) joined with the spec 02 field semantics. Re-run it whenever the registry or spec 02 changes; a field that exists in code but not here is a defect.

An explicit whitelist match overrides the blacklist; dynamic IP bans still apply. null (not empty) means "no whitelist". blacklist blacklist str list (IP/CIDR) [] Blocked IPs/CIDRs. Enforced ahead of country and cloud checks; overridden by an explicit whitelist match. Entries normalized to canonical form. ## Redis / distributed state Field Kotlin property Type Default Effect enable_redis enableRedis bool true Enables distributed state (shared bans, counters, caches). Valid categories: the penetration-detection categories (see enabled_detection_categories) plus the pseudo-category "rate_limit". Unknown category keys: rejected. Unlisted categories fall back to the flat thresholds. enable_rate_limit_auto_ban enableRateLimitAutoBan bool false Feed rate-limit violations into the auto-ban engine: each active-mode violation increments the "rate_limit" suspicious count and runs the same threshold logic (threat_ban_config["rate_limit"] first, then flat). Requires enable_ip_banning to actually ban. ## Geo / countries Field Kotlin property Type Default Effect whitelist_countries whitelistCountries str set (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) [] Non-empty = restrictive: only listed countries pass; unresolved country is blocked. Overrides blocked_countries (setting both warns). blocked_countries blockedCountries str set [] Countries always blocked. geo_ip_handler geoIpHandler handler or none null GeoIP provider (section 01 surface). Auto-resolved at validation when country rules exist and this is null (see Validation semantics). ipinfo_token ipinfoToken str or none null IPInfo API token for geolocation download. ipinfo_db_path ipinfoDbPath path "data/ipinfo/country_asn.mmdb" Local MMDB file path. geo_ip_db_max_age geoIpDbMaxAge int, 3600–604800 (ge=3600, le=604800) 86400 Max age in seconds of the IPInfo MMDB before re-download. ## Cloud providers Field Kotlin property Type Default Effect block_cloud_providers blockCloudProviders str set or none null Providers to block. Valid names: AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean, Linode, Vultr. A bare name blocks the whole provider; "<name>:!<region>" blocks the provider except that region. Region data exists for AWS and GCP only; a carve-out on other providers exempts nothing. Unknown provider names: rejected. cloud_ip_refresh_interval cloudIpRefreshInterval int, 60–86400 (ge=60, le=86400) 3600 Seconds between cloud IP range refreshes. cloud_ip_store cloudIpStore store instance, store factory, or none null Override for the shared cloud-IP cache (section 01 surface). null = auto-construct the Redis-backed store when Redis is enabled. A factory is a callable taking the redis handler and returning a store (defers construction). lazy_init lazyInit bool true Defer cloud-IP HTTP fetches and geo MMDB downloads to a background task. Effective only when Redis is enabled AND the adapter wires the deferred-init startup hook; otherwise cloud/geo init happens on demand and this flag is inert. First requests may see partially populated ranges. ## Rate limiting Field Kotlin property Type Default Effect enable_rate_limiting enableRateLimiting bool true Master switch for rate limiting. rate_limit rateLimit int 10 Max requests per rate_limit_window. rate_limit_window rateLimitWindow int 60 Window in seconds. endpoint_rate_limits endpointRateLimits map of endpoint str → (requests int, window int) {} Per-endpoint overrides; normally populated by dynamic rules. ## Detection / penetration Field Kotlin property Type Default Effect enable_penetration_detection enablePenetrationDetection bool true Master switch. enabled_detection_categories enabledDetectionCategories str set all categories Subset of: xss, sqli, dir_traversal, path_traversal, cmd_injection, file_inclusion, ldap, xml, ssrf, nosql, file_upload, template, http_split, sensitive_file, cms_probing, recon, proto_pollution, code_injection, deserialization. Unknown names: rejected. Empty set while detection is on: warning (detection enabled but never matches). excluded_detection_headers excludedDetectionHeaders str set {} Headers exempted from the categories known to false-positive on their typical values (identity/proxy headers skip ssrf only); other categories still scan them. Merged with the hardcoded default exclusion set. excluded_detection_params excludedDetectionParams str set {} Query parameters excluded from detection scanning. excluded_detection_body_fields excludedDetectionBodyFields str set {} JSON body keys excluded from detection scanning, matched at any nesting depth; also applied to form-urlencoded and multipart text-part field names. detection_scan_body detectionScanBody bool true Scan the request body. False: detection restricted to path, query, headers; the body is never read. detection_max_body_inspect_bytes detectionMaxBodyInspectBytes int, 1024–10485760 (ge=1024, le=10485760) 262144 Max bytes read from the start of the request body for detection. Only this prefix is scanned; payloads beyond it, or split across the boundary, are not detected. Also bounds gzip-bomb decompression. Without a bounded body reader (section 01.2), the body is not read at all and detection falls back to path/query/headers; either way a one-time warning names the cap, the client, and which happened. detection_max_content_length detectionMaxContentLength int, 1000–100000 (ge=1000, le=100000) 10000 Budget for the semantic (ML) analyzer slice of preprocessed content and the divisor for retained attack-indicator regions during truncation. Does NOT bound the regex scan window (that is detection_max_body_inspect_bytes). detection_max_scan_values detectionMaxScanValues int, 2–100000 (ge=2, le=100000) 512 Max individual values (query params, header values, JSON keys/leaf values, form fields, multipart parts) scanned per request; each value costs two units (name + value). Beyond the cap, remaining values are not scanned; one-time warning names the client IP. detection_max_scan_chars detectionMaxScanChars int, 1024–262144 (ge=1024, le=262144) 65536 Max total characters across every value handed to the pattern engine per request. Beyond the cap: same fail-open + warning as above. detection_max_json_depth detectionMaxJsonDepth int, 1–1000 (ge=1, le=1000) 32 Max JSON nesting depth walked structurally. docs.title: Detection
docs.text: What the engine detects, under which category names, and - just as important - what it cannot detect. The category names are the interop surface (spec 06): ports must not rename them, and neither do the adapters.

docs.title: Coverage taxonomy
docs.text:
ALL_DETECTION_CATEGORIES contains exactly these 19 category strings (verbatim, spec 06):

xss, sqli, dir_traversal, path_traversal, cmd_injection, file_inclusion,
ldap, xml, ssrf, nosql, file_upload, template, http_split, sensitive_file,
cms_probing, recon, proto_pollution, code_injection, deserialization

Two additional category strings exist outside the set:

  • "custom": every user-added pattern, and the synthetic decode-budget threat.
  • Semantic threats carry attack_type (not category); when a category is derived for events they map through the reference's semantic-to-category table (xss->xss, sql->sqli, command->cmd_injection, path->path_traversal, template->template, suspicious->custom; any other value passes through unchanged).

Categories scan source contexts (url_path, query_param, header, request_body, unknown) per the spec 06 context table: cmd_injection, file_upload, sensitive_file, cms_probing, and recon skip one context each (url_path for the first two, header for the last three).

Configuration knobs: enabled_detection_categories, excluded_detection_headers, excluded_detection_params, excluded_detection_body_fields, and the threshold family - all documented in Configuration under Detection / penetration.

docs.title: Detection limits (bounded reads)
docs.text:
These limits are part of the contract (spec 01.2/01.4), not defects, and they are the honest operating envelope of every guard family port:

  • Bounded request read. When a request has no usable Content-Length (e.g. chunked encoding), the adapter's bounded body reader returns at most detection_max_body_inspect_bytes bytes from the start of the body, and implementations must not buffer more than that internally. Only the returned prefix is scanned: payloads beyond the cap, or signatures split across the boundary, are not detected. Absence of the capability is treated as "cannot bound the read": the engine never reads the full body as an implicit fallback - the body is not read at all and a one-time warning names the cap, the client, and which of the two happened.
  • Bounded response read. Behavioral return_pattern rules with behavior_scan_response_body enabled read at most behavior_max_response_body_inspect_bytes of the outgoing body, teed so the full body still reaches the client, and never by consuming the underlying stream (indefinite streams such as SSE yield whatever prefix is available at a natural stopping point). Without the bounded response capability, body-based return patterns are skipped entirely.
  • Scan budgets. detection_max_scan_values bounds the number of individual values scanned per request and detection_max_scan_chars the total characters handed to the pattern engine; beyond a cap the remainder is not scanned (fail-open with a one-time warning naming the client IP). detection_max_json_depth bounds structural JSON walking; at the cap the value is serialized and scanned as one value.

Every limit is enforced with the same posture: the engine prefers under-scanning with a warning over unbounded reads, and the corpus (safety_gates suite) pins the warning and verdict behavior.

docs.title: Supported runtimes

• JDK 17 or newer (the build pins the JVM toolchain to 17; adapters test on 17). Spring Boot 3.x and Ktor 3.x both require Java 17+, so the family baseline is 17.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
Maven Central (published at release; pre-release builds come from source):

dependencies {
    // the facade: one artifact with config, pipeline, handlers, protocols
    implementation("com.guard-core:guard-core:4.3.2")
    // framework-free detection engine only (no coroutines/redis deps)
    implementation("com.guard-core:guard-core-engine:4.3.2")
}

The group ID is com.guard-core (the Central Portal namespace; it reverses to guard-core.com). Kotlin packages stay com.guardcore.* (hyphens are illegal in package names; the groupId/package mismatch is standard for hyphenated domains).

Adapters normally consume the adapter artifact, not the facade directly:

implementation("com.guard-core:spring-boot-guard:1.0.0") // Spring Boot 3.x
implementation("com.guard-core:ktor-guard:1.0.0")        // Ktor 3.x

git clone https://github.com/Guard-Core/guard-core-jvm.git
cd guard-core-jvm

docs.title: Redis requirement
docs.text: Distributed features (shared rate limiting, IP bans, behavioral state) need a Redis 6+ server configured through redis_url (default redis://localhost:6379). Set enable_redis = false to run without Redis: all state is per-process. The conformance corpus's redis_interop suite additionally asserts the Redis key schema byte-exact against a live server (CI pins redis:7-alpine).

docs.title: Version catalog
docs.text: All third-party pins live in gradle/libs.versions.toml and are locked: gradle.lockfile per module is committed, and a dependency change without ./gradlew --write-locks fails the build (the supply-chain frozen-lock rule).

docs.title: No prior JVM version exists
docs.text: guard-core-jvm is a fresh port family: the first stable release is the current 4.3.2 mirror line, and no earlier JVM major version exists to migrate from. Nothing was ever published under the interim com.guardcore group ID (see the CHANGELOG's groupId note), so there is no coordinate migration either. Consumers adopt at com.guard-core:guard-core:4.3.2 or through an adapter.

docs.title: Porting from another guard family
docs.text:
Behavior is identical across the family (that is the parity bar): the same verdicts, status codes, headers, Redis key schema, and event surfaces. When moving an existing deployment from the Python, Go, Rust, TypeScript, or PHP family to the JVM:

  • Configuration translates 1:1 through the canonical snake_case field names (Configuration lists every field with its Kotlin property; adapters map them idiomatically).
  • The section 08 Redis state schema is byte-compatible across the family: a JVM deployment can take over the Redis state an existing family member wrote (same key names, prefixes, and serialization), subject to the mixed-version constraints below.
  • Detection coverage and category names are identical; the JVM compiles the corpus patterns as-is (158-entry pattern ledger, zero translations).

docs.title: Mixed-version interop constraints
docs.text: The section 08 state format is the cross-language contract and changes only with a spec version bump. Such changes are documented in the CHANGELOG (targeting the spec version) and in Release notes before release, and they are the SECURITY-adjacent interop constraints to check before rolling a JVM port into an existing mixed-family Redis fleet.

docs.title: Deprecations
docs.text: Deprecated config fields or checks are documented in the CHANGELOG with their replacement and the removal target version. At the 4.3.2 baseline there are no deprecations.

docs.title: Release notes
docs.text:
Release notes live in the repository CHANGELOG.

Conventions (family-wide, matching the reference repo):

  • Every release entry states the spec version targeted and, for engine releases, the mirrored guard-core version.
  • Engine and facade versions move in lockstep with guard-core (4.3.2); the adapters start a fresh family version at 1.0.0; the agent mirrors guard-agent (3.2.2).
  • Breaking behavior changes (spec version bumps) and mixed-version Redis interop constraints (section 08) are documented in the CHANGELOG and in Migration before release.

docs.title: 2. Auth-path decision and what is pending (operator)
docs.text:
Verified (2026-10-11, central.sonatype.org Publisher API docs + release notes):

  • The Central Portal Publisher API authenticates with a Portal user token (Authorization: Bearer base64(username:password)). The workflows are built for this path via four secrets: CENTRAL_PORTAL_USERNAME, CENTRAL_PORTAL_PASSWORD, GPG_PRIVATE_KEY, GPG_PASSPHRASE.
  • OIDC trusted publishing does not exist for Maven Central (npm/PyPI/ Packagist have it; Maven does not). Therefore the publish jobs carry contents: read only and no id-token scope. If Sonatype ships trusted publishing, that is a follow-up, not a blocker.
  • GPG signing is mandatory (every file needs .asc; proven in 1.5).
  • New publishing limits took effect 2026-10-01 (announced 2026-06-16, enforcement pushed from Aug 11; 30-day grace): three monthly per-org metrics (file count, release size, release count), Usage Center is the source of truth. This family is orders of magnitude below the thresholds.

Pending on the operator (each blocks the corresponding step of docs/release.md):

  1. Portal user token generated and the two CENTRAL_PORTAL_* secrets set on all four repos. Blocks: the publish jobs' credential gate.
  2. GPG key pair created, the public key uploaded to a keyserver (the Portal validates against the keyserver copy), and the armored secret key + passphrase set as GPG_PRIVATE_KEY / GPG_PASSPHRASE on all four repos (4 secrets per repo in total, counting the two Portal ones). Blocks: the publish jobs' GPG gate (and Portal validation).
  3. GitHub releases created per tag at train time (the publish jobs fire on release: created, not on the tag push alone). Blocks: publishing only.

RESOLVED (was pending item 1): the Portal namespace com.guard-core flipped to VERIFIED 2026-10-11 16:15 (Portal badge, Org Guard-core). History: com.guardcore was abandoned 2026-10-11 (guardcore.com is a parked domain the operator does not own, making that claim unverifiable); com.guard-core reverses to the owned guard-core.com; the operator re-registered, swapped the apex TXT to the new verification key, and the Portal validated it.

docs.title: 3. Remaining operator steps (release day, condensed)
docs.text:
The full choreography is docs/release.md; the condensed checklist:

  1. Confirm the Portal shows com.guard-core Verified; secrets set on all four repos (section 2 items 1-2); Usage Center clean.
  2. Engine: tag v4.3.2 on a green master -> gates green -> create the GitHub release -> publish job uploads + VALIDATES both deployments (engine first, facade second) -> click Release on both in the Portal UI -> repo1 answers 200 for both artifacts.
  3. Adapters + agent, in any order (each guarded by its own pre-flight): version-flip PR merged (1.0.0-SNAPSHOT -> 1.0.0, 3.2.2-SNAPSHOT -> 3.2.2; CHANGELOG ## [SEMVER] - YYYY-MM-DD) -> tag -> release created -> pre-flight proves the engine live -> publish -> Portal release -> repo1 200.
  4. Post-release audits (per tag): GitHub release page exists; repo1 200 per artifact; no deployment left VALIDATED/PENDING in the Portal; Usage Center clean. Then move the consumers' pinned engine refs to the released engine SHA in the next regular development PR.

Rollback: before the Portal click, Drop the deployment (nothing published); after the click there is no undo - only a fix version (artifacts are immutable; tags of published versions never get deleted).

docs.title: Release runbook (guard-core-jvm)
docs.text: The exact choreography for the operator on release day. NOTHING releases without fresh explicit operator go (W8b standing rule): every step below is a deliberate human action. This document covers the engine repo; the adapters (spring-boot-guard, ktor-guard) and the agent (guard-agent-jvm) have their own runbooks with the same structure and a version-flip checklist.

docs.title: Versioning law
docs.text:
Artifact Repo Version Rule guard-core-engine guard-core-jvm (this repo) 4.3.2 lockstep with guard-core 4.3.2 guard-core (facade) guard-core-jvm (this repo) 4.3.2 lockstep with guard-core 4.3.2 spring-boot-guard spring-boot-guard 1.0.0 fresh family version ktor-guard ktor-guard 1.0.0 fresh family version guard-agent-jvm guard-agent-jvm 3.2.2 mirrors guard-agent 3.2.2
  • The engine version is set in-file (build.gradle.kts, allprojects). Tags must match it exactly: the engine tags v4.3.2.
  • Tags are bare vX.Y.z only: no suffixes (v4.3.2-jvm is wrong), no build metadata. The tag-consistency job refuses anything else. This audit exists because of the guard-core-rs invisible-rule incident on refs/tags/v4.3.2.
  • CHANGELOG entries use ## [SEMVER] - YYYY-MM-DD and mirror the narrative naming of the guard-core Python repo.
  • groupId com.guard-core (the Maven Central Portal namespace; it reverses to guard-core.com). Kotlin/JVM packages stay com.guardcore.*: hyphens are illegal in JVM packages and the groupId/package mismatch is standard for hyphenated domains.

docs.title: Publishing auth reality (verified 2026-10-11)
docs.text:
• The Central Portal Publisher API authenticates with a Portal user token (Authorization: Bearer base64(username:password)), generated in the Portal under Account -> Generate User Token. OIDC trusted publishing does not exist for Maven Central as of October 2026 (npm/PyPI/Packagist have it; Maven does not): the publish jobs therefore request no id-token scope and are the least-privilege set. If Sonatype ships trusted publishing later, this section and the workflows get a follow-up.
  • GPG signing is mandatory. Every deployed file needs an .asc signature. The key never leaves the runner: the workflow passes the armored private key + passphrase through Gradle's useInMemoryPgpKeys.
  • Checksums .md5/.sha1 are mandatory (.sha256/.sha512 optional); Gradle's maven-publish generates them.
  • Sources and javadoc jars are mandatory for every artifact (the build files produce them; the javadoc jar carries the README until Dokka lands).
  • Publishing limits took effect 2026-10-01: three monthly metrics per organization (file count, release size, release count), evaluated as hard thresholds with a grace flow. The source of truth for thresholds and usage is the Portal's Usage Center. A JVM family train (4 deployments, well under 100 files) is far below the community thresholds; check the Usage Center before each train anyway.
  • Publishing type is fixed to USER_MANAGED in the workflows: deployments are uploaded and VALIDATED by CI, and a human releases them from the Portal UI. This is the deliberate human gate before artifacts go immutable-live. (AUTOMATIC would skip that gate; do not switch without an operator ruling.)

docs.text:
1. Portal namespace com.guard-core shows Verified at central.sonatype.com. (History: the com.guardcore claim was abandoned as unverifiable on 2026-10-11 - guardcore.com is a parked domain the operator does not own; com.guard-core reverses to guard-core.com, TXT record placed, re-registered 2026-10-11. repo1.maven.org has no prior art for either group.)
  2. Generate a Portal user token (Account -> Generate User Token).
  3. Prepare the signing key, if none exists yet:
  4. gpg --full-generate-key (RSA 4096, no expiry is fine, email rennf93@guard-core.com).
  5. Distribute the public key: gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --send-key <KEYID> (Portal validation checks public availability).
  6. Export for CI: gpg --armor --export-secret-keys <KEYID>.
  7. Set four GitHub secrets on each family repo (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions):
Secret Value CENTRAL_PORTAL_USERNAME user token username CENTRAL_PORTAL_PASSWORD user token password GPG_PRIVATE_KEY armored private key (whole -----BEGIN ... KEY BLOCK----- block) GPG_PASSPHRASE the key's passphrase

docs.title: Release choreography (family order)
docs.text: Engine first, then the Portal release clicks, then (and only then) the adapters and the agent.

docs.title: 1. Engine (this repo)
docs.text:
1. Confirm build.gradle.kts carries the release version (4.3.2 - no flip needed while in lockstep; the version lives in the file, never on the command line) and the CHANGELOG has a ## [4.3.2] - YYYY-MM-DD section.
  2. Tag on the release commit: git tag v4.3.2 && git push origin v4.3.2. The tag push runs the gate suite (build + full-corpus certification + tag-consistency audit). Wait for it to go green.
  3. Create the GitHub release for v4.3.2 (Create release from the tag). The release: created event starts the publish job:
  4. secrets gate -> existence check per artifact (skip if already live) -> guard-core-engine staging bundle -> Portal upload -> VALIDATED -> guard-core staging bundle -> Portal upload -> VALIDATED (engine-before-facade is enforced by job structure; a partial failure re-drives with workflow_dispatch and only the missing artifact publishes).
  5. In the Portal UI (central.sonatype.com, Publishing -> Deployments): inspect both VALIDATED deployments, then click Release on the engine deployment first, the facade second.
  6. Wait for replication and verify liveness (this is the signal the consumer releases wait on):
  7. curl -f https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/guard-core/guard-core-engine/4.3.2/guard-core-engine-4.3.2.pom
  8. curl -f https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/guard-core/guard-core/4.3.2/guard-core-4.3.2.pom

docs.title: 2. Adapters and agent (spring-boot-guard, ktor-guard, guard-agent-jvm)
docs.text:
Only after step 1.5 succeeds (their workflows re-check it anyway):

  1. Version-flip PR per repo (see the checklist below): flip the project version, update the CHANGELOG, merge with CI green.
  2. Tag: git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0 (agent: v3.2.2). Gates run: engine-artifact pre-flight, tests at tag, tag-consistency.
  3. Create the GitHub release. The publish job runs with GUARD_CORE_USE_COMPOSITE=false, so the build resolves com.guard-core:guard-core:4.3.2 from Maven Central (mavenLocal, then Central) - proving the published graph, not the composite checkout.
  4. Release the VALIDATED deployment in the Portal UI.
  5. Verify liveness:
  6. curl -f https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/guard-core/spring-boot-guard/1.0.0/spring-boot-guard-1.0.0.pom
  7. curl -f https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/guard-core/ktor-guard/1.0.0/ktor-guard-1.0.0.pom
  8. curl -f https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/guard-core/guard-agent-jvm/3.2.2/guard-agent-jvm-3.2.2.pom

docs.title: Version-flip checklist (adapters + agent, per release PR)
docs.text:
• [ ] build.gradle.kts: version = "1.0.0-SNAPSHOT" -> version = "1.0.0" (agent: 3.2.2-SNAPSHOT -> 3.2.2).
  • [ ] gradle/libs.versions.toml: the guardCore version ref still reads 4.3.2 (the lockstep engine pin - bump it only when the engine train moves).
  • [ ] CHANGELOG.md: rename the Unreleased section to ## [1.0.0] - YYYY-MM-DD and state the engine pin.
  • [ ] The workflow's tag-consistency job is the safety net: it fails with a clear message if the tag is pushed without the flip (SNAPSHOT version) or if the tag does not equal the in-file version.
  • [ ] The consumers' GUARD_CORE_JVM_REF pins (ci.yml + settings comments) already point at the released engine SHA: they bump AT TRAIN TIME, before the consumer tags, so the at-tag tests run against the engine that actually ships (the family spec pins this; a pin bump is an ordinary development PR).

docs.title: Post-release audits (per train, per tag - the php v4.3.1 lesson)
docs.text:
1. Release page audit: every tag in the train has a GitHub release page with the expected artifact notes and no draft leftovers.
  2. Registry existence check: every artifact coordinates above answers HTTP 200 on repo1 (the same check the workflows use for rerun safety).
  3. Portal Deployments audit: no deployment left in VALIDATED/PENDING.
  4. Usage Center: the train registered without warnings.

docs.title: Rerun safety and failure recovery
docs.text:
• A publish job that dies mid-train re-drives via workflow_dispatch: the existence check skips anything already live on repo1, and only the missing deployment uploads again.
  • A deployment stuck in VALIDATED that you do NOT want: click Drop in the Portal UI, then re-drive the workflow.
  • Validation FAILED: the job logs print the Portal's error messages; fix the POM/jar/signature issue, drop the failed deployment in the Portal, re-drive.
  • Workflow re-runs NEVER double-publish: repo1 serving 200 is authoritative.

docs.title: Rollback notes
docs.text:
• Published Maven Central artifacts are immutable and undeleteable. There is no rollback after the Portal Release click - only a fixed follow-up version.
  • The rollback surface that exists:
  • Before the click: Drop the VALIDATED deployment (nothing was published).
  • After the click: cut a fix version through the same choreography, and (for security-grade breakage) yank consumers off the artifact via a patch release of the adapters plus a documented advisory.
  • Delete the git tag and GitHub release only for a train that never released (no VALIDATED deployment was released); a published artifact's tag must stay forever.

docs.title: Rehearsal
docs.text: The W8b dry-run proof (publishToMavenLocal, POM validation, workflow lint) and its findings live in docs/release-rehearsal.md. The rehearsal never touched a remote registry: the first real upload happens only on operator go, on release day, through the choreography above.

docs.title: Idiom mappings (syntax, not substitutes)
docs.text:
1. asyncio -> blocking engine + worker hop: python's async detect and the shared regex executor map to a synchronous detect() executed on one 512 MiB-stack scan-pool worker. Coroutine bridges land in the facade (W4) per the work order's unasync ruling.
  2. killable subprocess -> hard deadline: the reference times probes and verifies strays in killable subprocesses; the JVM analog is the DeadlineCharSequence abort (PyRe.DeadlineExceededException carries the reference's TimeoutError semantics and the reason strings name the same classes: "killable-subprocess timeout" texts kept verbatim for ledger comparability).
  3. sre internals -> PyReParser/PyAst: python's re._parser grammar and ast.parse(mode= "eval") are CPython-internal; the JVM ports reproduce the accept/reject oracle fail-closed (ReParseError message classes verbatim; PyAst = eval-mode expression grammar).
  4. pickle._Unpickler -> opcode table: the blocked-resolution exceptions map to explicit raises in the modeled dispatch; a raise means "not a provable opcode stream" exactly as the reference's exception-to-False conversions.

docs.text:
• redis.asyncio.Redis -> Lettuce StatefulRedisConnection behind the RedisOperations interface; pipeline(transaction=True) -> MULTI/EXEC with per-command futures read in order. The redis-py client-level retry (Retry(ExponentialBackoff(), retries), redis_handler.py:116) maps to the Lettuce reconnect/timeout options: transient failures surface as GuardRedisError(503, ...) after the timeout budget either way.
  • cachetools.TTLCache -> handlers/TtlCache.kt (expiry-ordered eviction, lazy purge, injectable clock standing in for cachetools timer).

  • maxminddb.open_database -> com.maxmind.db:maxmind-db reader with a @MaxMindDbConstructor country record projection.
  • Mixins -> one class per python module group with internal/open members; _apply_blocking_rules and the application steps are open members so the python test idiom of overriding a step to drive the rollback path ports verbatim (ScriptedStepManager in the tests).
  • asyncio singletons (__new__-based) -> companion getInstance with resetInstance() test seams.
  • monkeypatch.setattr(manager, "ban_ip", fake) -> assertions against the real ban store (local TTL cache expiry) since Kotlin extension dispatch is static; durations pinned below the 3600s local cache cap to keep the same distinguishing power.
  • asyncio.create_task (ipinfo lookup-failure event) -> a manager-scope coroutine scope launch.

Route-id collision study (the guard-core #141/#142 class): the python bug was factory-built endpoints (closures sharing one __qualname__) deriving the same module.qualname route id, so one endpoint could select another's RouteConfig; python's defense (decorators/base.py:84-105) reuses a stamped id only when the SAME instance assigned it to the SAME function object (owner chain over id(func)/__wrapped__), else allocates key#2.

JVM capability comparison: route identity is caller-supplied object identity (StampedRoute carrying stampedRouteId, or a string key) - the analog of the TS WeakMap case. Two factory-built endpoints in the JVM are two distinct StampedRoute objects, so the derived-key collision class python had cannot occur: identical base keys get key#2-style suffixes per instance, and stamped ids are never reused across instances (the owner map). SecurityDecoratorTest (route-id collision campaign) ports tests/test_decorators/test_route_id_per_function.py 1:1: own-rate-limit isolation, settings not leaking, first endpoint keeps the plain key, stacked decorators share one config (the intentional case), and cross-instance stamped-id non-reuse.

docs.title: Certification-revealed engine bugs (fixed here, byte-exact, with tests)
docs.text:
1. StructureRules.isBroadCharClassInner double escape. The non-negated branch compared the Kotlin literal "\\\\s\\\\S" (runtime text \\s\\S, six chars) instead of the raw class inner text \s\S (python: inner in ("\\s\\S", "\\S\\s")), so [\s\S] was never counted as a broad atom. The adjacent-broad prefilter missed [\s\S]*[\s\S]+$ and [\s\S]*x[^%]+ (safety_test_strings_structural_adjacent_broad_05/06). Fixed to the python literal text; regression tests in RedosChainTest.
  2. PyRe.translateSource skipped the documented named-group translation. The verbatim path never applied (?P<name> -> (?<name> / (?P=name) -> \k<name>, so python-spelled named groups failed the compile gate in java.util.regex ("Unknown inline modifier") before the structural checks could classify - five corpus cases diverged to compile_failed. Fixed in the translator (class-aware: (?P< inside a character class stays literal); regression tests in PyReBehaviorTest.
  3. Cloud checks' applies_to missed the dynamic-rules disjunct. The reference cloud_blocking_enabled helper is bool(block_cloud_providers) or enable_dynamic_rules; the JVM CloudIpRefreshCheck/CloudProviderCheck companions checked only the providers set, so applies_to dropped both checks under enable_dynamic_rules with no providers configured. Found by the ported test_check_applies_to.py matrix; fixed and covered there.

All six are cost_verdict-mode timing facts: the corpus pins the reference engine's probe timings (python re on the generating host), and the arbiter certifies what THIS engine's executor (java.util.regex backtracking under the DeadlineCharSequence abort) measures on the same synthesized probe sets. The structural, compile, dangerous-construct, and test-string-probe layers reproduce every reference verdict exactly.

The ledger accepts either outcome for those; any third verdict is red. The Go family documented the identical flip on safety_cost_verdict_safe_05 on its engine (guard-core#75 era transient note in the corpus refresh record).

docs.text:
1. util/DetectionScan.kt fallbackPatternCheck caught Exception per pattern; the reference catches ONLY RecursionError (detection_scan.py:216-222), logs the redacted pattern source, and continues.   2. util/DetectionScan.kt checkValueEnhanced routed every engine failure into the fallback branch; the reference re-raises RecursionError ahead of the generic handler (detection_scan.py:337-339). The engine pool delivers worker failures as ExecutionException, so the unwrap now rethrows a StackOverflowError cause ahead of the fallback. Regression: EdgeCasesTest.recursionClassFailureEscapesTheEnhancedFailureFallback pins the delivery shape and the fallback-layer catch.
  3. decorators/RouteConfig.kt shipped the tracked-container PORTS (TrackedList/TrackedMap/TrackedSet) without wiring them into the tracked fields, so IN-PLACE mutation of custom_validators, required_headers, blocked_user_agents, block_cloud_providers (and the assigned require_referrer/allowed_content_types/time_restrictions/geo_rate_limits payloads) never bumped the route-config revision - the exact rebuild trigger the revision system exists for (route_config.py:265-302). docs.title: Bugs found and fixed (byte-exact, with regression tests)
docs.text:
1. global_behavior_rules setter used the wrong revalidator (SecurityConfig.kt): python coerces dict entries to BehaviorRuleConfig at assignment (_validate_typed_collection_field_value with _GLOBAL_BEHAVIOR_RULES_ADAPTER, pinned by test_global_behavior_rules_reassignment_coerces_dicts_to_model); the JVM setter ran the str-list validator and DROPPED/REJECTED the entries. Fixed with ConfigValidators.validateGlobalBehaviorRulesFieldValue.
  2. nowSeconds() resolution = the recurring rate-limit zwrite loss (IpBanBans.kt): System.currentTimeMillis()/1000.0 has millisecond resolution, so two sliding-window zadd calls inside the same millisecond produce the same sorted-set member and the second write is a silent no-op. python time.time() has microsecond resolution and never collides. The work order's "RateLimitManager pipeline+primitive interleave zwrite loss" flake (3 recurrences this wave) is this bug. Fixed with an Instant-based nowSeconds.
  3. redis_interop runner: score_equals_member compared RAW STRINGS (RedisInteropTest.kt): the reference harness (redis_interop_cases.py:311-313) pins the rate-limit zset contract as NUMERIC equality within 1e-6 (abs(score - float(member)) < 1e-6) because the member is rendered by the redis-side Lua, whose float formatting is build-dependent (the docker redis builds emit e-notation for sub-microsecond timestamps; glibc/macOS builds render positionally). The nowSeconds fidelity fix (item 2) is what surfaced it. The verifier now ports the numeric contract, and the CI redis images were aligned to the redis 8 major the corpus is generated against (matching the python family pin image: redis).
  4. Test-suite state leak (SusPatternsRegistryTest): removed a DEFAULT pattern from the process-global table and never restored it, disabling one detection pattern for every suite running after it.

docs.title: Tests added this wave
docs.text:
• ValidationCacheTest: the disk-backed validation cache (put/get round trip, version filtering, corrupt/foreign-shape rejection, atomic write, the directory-as-path arm) + JsonMini (parse arms, string escapes, control-char rendering, every value kind, the JSON-null sentinel).

  • MonitorTest: every anomaly detector arm, event builders, reporting helpers, and the PerformanceMonitor lifecycle (truncation, clamping, eviction, agent sink emission, the per-pattern cooldown, callback failure error events, sink-failure swallowing, summary stats).
  • RedosProbesTest: load-factor and deadline scaling, verdict components, cost/unreachable reason text, timing-row validation arms, batched measurement (valid + null batches), probe-fill builders, reach synthesis, stray chooser.
  • EncodingTruncationTest: escape decoders (hex/unicode/percent-u/overlong UTF-8), base64 candidate decoding incl. gzip peeling, attack-region extraction/merging, safe truncation branches, ignorecase fold expansion, binary prefix/islands, PyUnicode tails.
  • CompilerSafetyTest: the cached compiler (LRU arms, eviction, sync compile), validatePatternSafety ordering (dangerous constructs -> compile -> cache -> probe), the probe timeout path, safe matchers under deadline, batch compilation.
  • ParseSlotsStructureTest: slot shapes, category predicates (ASCII + marks), the ambiguous-tail grammar, structure rules (broad shorthands are the uppercase S/W/D), structure primitives, unreachable-terminator detection, SemanticAnalyzer full surface, the preprocessor pipeline (decode budget exhaustion via a 20-deep nested percent encoding, signal-preserving views, sql-comment stripping), PyUrllib/PyHtml.
  • PyReParserErrorsTest: the sre_parse fail-closed arms (nothing/multiple repeat, overflowed repetition, unterminated sets, bad ranges, incomplete escapes, the \N gate, octal escapes, group references, named groups, inline flags incl. the global-flags position rule, the 20-nesting limit, verbose-mode comment skipping).
  • PyReTailsTest: translation edges (named groups, leading-] classes, {,m}, scoped (?-i:...) rewrite + capture, the LOCALE gate), the hard deadline (search abort + the periodic charAt tick), the match-group surface.
  • PyGrammarTailsTest: the PyAst expression grammar arms + PyUnicode helpers.
  • SusPatternsPickleTest: the pickle opcode VM (every opcode family through the prefix/suffix walkers, blocked globals, the injection predicate, the surrogateescape window mapping).
  • SusPatternsTailsTest + SusPatternsManagerTailTest: xml/xxe walkers, ldap null-byte and quote-splice matchers through the real table patterns (WINDOWED_PATTERN_FINDERS), template scan matchers, brace-expansion danger, threat helpers, legacy ipv4 decoding, the enhanced-state builder, and the manager lifecycle (add/remove bookkeeping, detect() threat shape, the decode-budget-exhaustion threat, semantic category mapping, the Quad destructuring).

docs.title: Bugs found and fixed (byte-exact, with regression tests)
docs.text:
1. Monitor anomaly cooldown compared raw nanoseconds against a seconds cooldown (Monitor.kt reserveAnomalyEmission): python times the window with time.monotonic() (seconds, monitor.py:197); the JVM fed System.nanoTime() straight in, making the suppression window 1e9x too small - every record re-emitted the anomaly to the agent sink. Fixed with the seconds analog. Regression: monitorAnomalyEmissionCooldownReservesPerPattern.
  2. positiveAssertion crashed on longer lookbehind witnesses (RepeatPrefixState.kt): python's state.text[: -len(witness.text)] yields "" when the witness exceeds the text (negative slice, _redos_repeat_prefix_state.py:101); the Kotlin substring threw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Fixed with the clamp. Anchored by the (?<=(X))\1 corpus shapes.
  3. Unterminated char classes crashed the structure scanners: python's reversed slices (pattern[i+1:j-1]) yield "" for a bare "[" (_redos_unreachable_terminator.py:77, _redos_structure_rules.py:58, _redos_structure_primitives.py); the Kotlin substring threw. Guarded at all five sites (UnreachableTerminator x2, StructureRules x2, StructurePrimitives x1).
  4. JsonMini coerced parsed JSON nulls to "" (ValidationCache.kt): python's json.loads preserves None and the load() shape checks reject a file with a null reason; the JVM accepted it as the empty string. A sentinel now preserves the null (cache-corruption contract).
  5. Atom-position 3-digit octal escapes parsed as group references (PyReParser.kt): "\\101" (octal 65 = 'A') became group reference 10 because the third-digit check peeked PAST the unconsumed digit (python's source.next is the char at the read position, sre_parse.py _escape). Fixed to peek().
  6. Overflowed brace-quantifier bounds silently became {0,0} (PyReParser.kt parseQuantifier): "x{99999999999}" must raise the repetition-number-too-large error (python MAXREPEAT check); the overflow flag only ran when parseDecimal returned null, but the overflow result carries parsed=false with a non-null Dec. Fixed.

docs.title: The fail-closed 100 percent line gate
docs.text:
scripts/enforce_line_coverage.sh + scripts/enforce_line_coverage.py (the guard-core-rs enforce_line_coverage.py analog):

  1. Downloads jacococli 0.8.15-nodeps if absent, VERIFYING THE SHA256 (d2b74b20b415163c1f53261e7c5ef4445b788327094208ff821e0c2baf9bc8f1); a mismatch aborts the gate.
  2. Runs ./gradlew test (every module).
  3. Merges ALL exec files against ALL modules' kotlin classes via jacococli (the merged method is load-bearing: per-module reports undercount cross-JVM execution).
  4. enforce_line_coverage.py fails (exit 1) unless the workspace total AND every module hold 100.0 percent covered lines, printing the uncovered-line ranges per class, attributed per module, on failure. JaCoCo excludes in the build config are only acceptable for genuinely unreachable arms and must carry a written reason next to the exclude.

Seeded-regression proof (run this wave): with ValidationCacheTest.kt removed, the engine test task stays green but the gate exits 1 and its report pins the exact uncovered lines:

guard-core-engine: covered 6737, missed 670, 90.9545% (threshold 100.00%)
[guard-core-engine] com/guardcore/engine/detection/ValidationCache.kt
    lines: 45-46, 74, 87, 123-129, 131, 141-145, ...

Restoring the test returns the engine to 91.68% (616 missed) and drops the class from the report. The gate catches a dropped/decayed test even when the test TASK stays green.

docs.title: ci.yml wiring (lands when the numbers hold)
docs.text:
The gate is NOT wired into ci.yml in this wave: the workspace is at 90.76%, and a red gate on master is worse than a missing gate. The follow-up wave closes the remaining 2,160 lines (the facade worklist in docs/w9a-coverage.md, the conformance runner arms, and the engine tail below), then adds one job to ci.yml, byte-for-byte:

coverage:
  name: coverage (100 percent line gate)
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  permissions:
    contents: read
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        persist-credentials: false
    - uses: actions/setup-java@de727f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
      with:
        distribution: temurin
        java-version: 17
    - name: Start Redis
      run: |
        docker run -d --name guard-redis -p 6379:6379 redis:8
        for i in $(seq 1 30); do
          if docker exec guard-redis redis-cli ping | grep -q PONG; then break; fi
          sleep 1
        done
    - name: Fail-closed 100 percent line-coverage gate
      run: scripts/enforce_line_coverage.sh
    - name: Stop Redis
      if: always()
      run: docker rm -f guard-redis || true

plus coverage added to the required contexts and to the paths filter.
